title: ARCH↔BACK-001: Edge–Cloud Contracts & Broker Topology + API/Scaling Feasibility
description: The Embedded Systems Architect provides the edge–cloud interface contracts, the MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) broker topology and QoS (Quality of Service), the device shadow/twin model, and the identity/provisioning topology; the Backend/Cloud Engineer provides API (Application Programming Interface) and broker feasibility, scaling limits, device-management constraints that may reshape the contract, and ADR proposals when a contract or topology is infeasible. Grounded in EMBEDDED_SYSTEMS_ARCHITECT_SKILL §6.8 and BACKEND_CLOUD_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.1. Scaling limits are validated against the fleet ceilings (SCALE-1 50,000 devices; SCALE-2 50,000 MQTT connections; SCALE-3 10,000 msgs/s); identity/provisioning topology is security-relevant (PKI under BACK↔SEC-001).

edge_cloud_architecture.description: ARCH→BACK: edge–cloud contracts, broker topology/QoS, device shadow/twin, identity/provisioning topology.

backend_feasibility.description: BACK→ARCH: API/broker feasibility, scaling limits, device-management constraints, infeasibility ADR.

x-macp.tier_rationale: Edge–cloud interface contracts, broker topology/QoS, device-twin and identity/provisioning topology are architecture decisions ratified by humans. An infeasible contract/topology is raised as an ADR; identity/provisioning topology is security-relevant (PKI binding under BACK↔SEC-001, ESC-SEC); scaling must be validated against the SCALE ceilings.
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER (contract handoff at planning; integration checkpoints; ADR consultation on any infeasibility; fleet-scaling review at production-ready)
confirm_conditions: scaling limits (max devices, max throughput) carry explicit units
the API/broker feasibility verdict is stated; INFEASIBLE carries an ADR reference
broker topology, QoS, device-twin and identity/provisioning topology are specified
scaling is reconciled against SCALE-1 (50,000 devices) / SCALE-2 / SCALE-3 (10,000 msgs/s)
reject_conditions: a scaling-limit quantity emitted without a unit (units rule §3.10)
a topology exceeding a SCALE ceiling presented as feasible without load validation (Honesty Over Polish §10.3)
a ratified edge–cloud contract / broker topology altered without a CCR + version bump
counter_conditions: the identity/provisioning topology change touches PKI/device identity — route the security decision through BACK↔SEC-001 (ESC-SEC) before committing
a device-management constraint reshapes the contract — request an ADR / Architect review before the topology is frozen
